previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, diabetes, and a history of failed kidney transplant was admitted for fevers and rigors that occurred during a dialysis session. He reported subjective low-grade fevers for about a week. Initial evaluation included a chest X-ray and ultrasound of the dialysis fistula, both of which showed no acute abnormalities. Blood cultures were negative for growth. He was treated with IV vancomycin and gentamicin initially, but antibiotics were discontinued as he improved clinically and remained afebrile. A vascular study revealed mild-to-moderate tibial occlusive disease, likely contributing to chronic foot ulcers. The patient stabilized, and after reassessment, was discharged home with instructions to continue follow-up with podiatry and manage his chronic conditions. No surgical procedures were performed during this admission.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Diabetes with renal manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled

radiology_notes.text:
PICC LINE PLACEMENT

INDICATION:  IV access needed for antibiotics.

The procedure was explained to the patient.  A timeout was performed.

RADIOLOGIST:  Dr. ___, Dr. ___, and Dr. ___
the procedure.

TECHNIQUE:  Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the right brachial
vein was punctured under direct ultrasound guidance using a micropuncture set.
Ultrasound images were obtained before and immediately after establishing
intravenous access.  A peel-away sheath was then placed over a guidewire and a
single-lumen PICC line measuring 46 cm in length was then placed through the
peel-away sheath.  At this point, there was difficulty advancing the PICC over
the wire in the upper arm.  The PICC and wire were removed and a Kumpe
catheter and 0.018 nitinol wire were advanced into the arm.  A small amount of
Visipaque contrast was injected which did not demonstrate any venous stenosis
in the upper right arm.  After this, the Kumpe catheter was easily advanced
slightly more proximally and the 0.018 nitinol wire was placed into the IVC. 
The Kumpe catheter was removed and the PICC was placed over the nitinol wire
and into the SVC with its tip positioned in the distal SVC.  
Position of the catheter was confirmed by a fluoroscopic spot film of the
chest.

The peel-away sheath and nitinol wire were then removed.  The catheter was
secured to the skin, flushed, and a sterile dressing applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well.  There were no immediate
complications.

IMPRESSION:  
Uncomplicated ultrasound and fluoroscopically guided single-lumen PICC line
placement via the right brachial venous approach.  
Final internal length is 46 cm, with the tip positioned in SVC.  
The line is ready to use.
